questions.question: She said she would have finished the project by Friday if she had received the additional resources sooner. What does this sentence imply about her original timeline?
options: She was confident she would finish on time despite the lack of resources.
She was certain she would not finish on time without the extra help.
She planned to start the project later than originally scheduled.
The additional resources were provided before she expected them.

questions.question: The meeting _______ at 3 PM yesterday, but the participants were late due to traffic.
options: had been scheduled
was being held
was to be cancelled
had just started

questions.question: He mentioned that he’d *never* seen a film quite like *that* before. Which collocation best fits the sentence?
options: seen a film *as* dramatic as this
seen a film *so* thrilling as this
seen a film *as* gripping as this
seen a film *as* suspenseful as this

questions.question: The manager insisted that the project *should have been completed* by the end of last week. Which of the following best paraphrases the implied criticism?
options: The project was delayed due to lack of resources.
The team failed to meet the original deadline despite adequate support.
The manager underestimated the complexity of the task.
The project was abandoned before completion.

questions.question: After *having spent* two hours researching, she concluded that the evidence was inconclusive. Which preposition best fits the sentence?
options: After *spending* two hours researching, she concluded...
After *spent* two hours researching, she concluded...
After *spend* two hours researching, she concluded...
After *having* spent two hours researching, she concluded...

questions.question: The new policy *aims to reduce* carbon emissions by encouraging public transport use. What does this sentence suggest about the government’s approach?
options: The policy is purely symbolic and has no real impact.
The government is taking immediate action to combat climate change.
Public transport is already widely used, so this policy is unnecessary.
The policy will only affect wealthy residents.

questions.question: He said that if *I had asked* him for advice, he *would have helped*. What is the most accurate interpretation of the implied meaning?
options: He regrets not offering help when asked.
He would have helped if he had been asked, but he didn’t.
He never intended to provide advice in the first place.
He believes he should have asked first before offering help.

questions.question: The book *was written* by a famous author, but it *has been translated* into ten languages. Which of the following best describes the passive structure here?
options: The author is still alive and working on translations.
The translations were done after the book was published.
The book’s popularity led to multiple translations.
The translations are ongoing, with more to come.

questions.question: She *must have been* exhausted after working all night. Which of the following best explains the use of *must have been*?
options: She definitely worked all night.
She probably worked all night, but it’s uncertain.
She worked all night, but she didn’t feel tired.
She worked all night, and her exhaustion was obvious.

questions.question: The scientist *proposed that further research* *be conducted* to understand the cause of the phenomenon. Which of the following best paraphrases the sentence?
options: The scientist suggested that more studies be done to explain the phenomenon.
The scientist argued that research should be stopped to avoid further experiments.
The scientist insisted that the phenomenon be studied immediately.
The scientist believed that the phenomenon was already well understood.
